subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: steady vs crest windows & streaming constraints
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@novaflow.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Oct 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: throughput & latency targets (action items)

Hey Samir — great catch-up earlier. Quick recap and asks so we can lock sizing for the pilot: 

Summary from our call:
- Latency SLO target: p95 <= 250ms (interactive product path).
- Steady-state profile: ~20 QPS sustained during business hours.
- Average payload: ~1.2k tokens/request (user prompt + context).
- Peak/crest windows: brief spikes up to ~6k QPS but typically for 2–5 minute bursts tied to batch ingest jobs.
- Streaming requirements: streaming responses for long completions; clients open long-lived connections (~30–90s).

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm the crest-window duration distribution (typical, 95th, max)? the sample trace you promised would help.
2) Please upload a 1–2 hour traffic trace (anonymized) or the CSV token profile you mentioned.
3) For the pilot, do you need guaranteed dedicated capacity or is a canary on hosted OK initially?

Attached: novaflow_token_profile.csv (example token histogram). I flagged the areas that drive high token/sec.

Next steps: once we have the trace I’ll run a quick sizing pass (tokens/sec aggregation + batching assumptions) and share a recommended config (batch sizes, concurrency, streaming buffer strategy) and a cost estimate. Can we aim for a follow-up on Tue (Oct 17) to review results?

Cheers,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: novaflow_token_profile.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Samir Shah <samir@novaflow.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina@novaflow.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & latency targets (action items)

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers and clarification below.

- Crest windows: typically 2–4 minutes, tied to our hourly batch job that fans out requests after ingestion. 95th is ~3.5 minutes; we've observed a rare max of ~8 minutes during data reprocesses.
- Steady-state: 18–22 QPS globally (US-heavy).
- Peak numbers: we quoted ~6k QPS earlier — that's the instantaneous TPS during the 90s crest in some regions; globally aggregated peaks can reach ~8–9k for 30–60s if multiple regions overlap.
- Token distribution: attached sample_trace_20281012.json has 90 minutes of anonymized request logs and token counts; average tokens/request ~1.15k, 95th ~4.8k.

Regarding capacity: for the pilot we prefer a hosted canary with a path to Dedicated within 2–4 weeks if sizing confirms. We'll need a cost estimate for both (hosted + dedicated reserved). Procurement is looped in for the budget.

Let me know if you need any additional fields in the trace (client_id, region tag).

—Samir
Senior Product Manager | NovaFlow
samir@novaflow.ai

Attachments: sample_trace_20281012.json (json, 1.1MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Oct 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call recap: throughput & latency targets (action items) — internal ops ask

Jonas / Karthik — forwarding Samir's trace. Highlights and proposed internal plan: 

Highlights from Samir's trace:
- Sustained window: ~20 QPS -> ~23k tokens/sec aggregate (20 * 1.15k).
- Common crest behavior: 2–4 minute bursts at regional peaks up to ~6k QPS; global overlaps can briefly hit ~8–9k.
- Long-tail tokens: 95th token/request ~4.8k — streaming is required for those.

Proposed sizing assumptions (for initial pilot):
- Model: rwd-4x-quant (recommended by infra for cost/latency tradeoff).
- Target concurrency per instance: 12 streaming sessions (given average completion length).
- Batching: dynamic batching with max batch size tuned to keep p95 under 250ms; expect batching to reduce per-token cost by ~18% on steady-state.
- Buffering strategy: enable prefix KV caching for repeated context; stream chunked responses for >2k tokens.

Asks:
- Jonas: can you run a quick capacity simulation (tokens/sec -> GPU instance count) with the attached token histogram and 250ms p95 goal? Include both steady and crest-headroom (x1.5 for safety).
- Karthik: prepare a two-line cost estimate (hosted canary hourly + Dedicated monthly commit) and a runbook for escalation if crest windows exceed predicted concurrency.

I’ll draft the pilot config and a short runbook to share with Samir before Tue’s call.

Thanks — Marissa

Attachments: redwood-serving-recommendation.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@novaflow.ai>, Lina Park <lina@novaflow.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@novaflow.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Oct 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: throughput & latency targets (action items) — pilot next steps

Samir / Lina — thanks for the trace and clarity. Confirming next steps and owners: 

1) We will run sizing sim and publish recommended pilot config by EOD Mon (Oct 23). Owner: Marissa (me) + Jonas for infra sim.
2) Karthik will send a hosted canary + Dedicated commit estimate by Wed (Oct 18). Owner: Karthik.
3) Tech validation call to review sizing & latency plan: Tue Oct 24, 10:00am PT — I’ll send calendar invite.
4) Procurement: please confirm preferred billing cadence and any PO template requirements ahead of Wed.

Notes: we’ll size for steady-state + 1.5x crest headroom and include a fallback policy to a slightly lower-capacity model if a true global super-crest happens. Attached is a short recommendation doc (redwood-serving-recommendation.pdf) that outlines batching/concurrency knobs we plan to use.

If that all looks good I’ll attach the pilot config and cost delta sheet once Jonas and Karthik finish their runs.

Best,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-serving-recommendation.pdf
